Composable UI kit

Reference Last updated: 2026-11-18

The composable C++ immediate-mode kit used by the runtime and legacy plugins.

This kit belongs to the runtime and legacy C++/ImGui host, not the active Rust Doppio. A panel is a tree of objects, cards and controls; plugins use the same model so their panels look like the host's native panels. The Rust editor uses Iced components and uikit/theme.rs instead.

Objects → Cards → Panels#

text
Panel
  └─ Card
       ├─ Toolbar
       │    ├─ Button
       │    └─ IconButton
       ├─ Row
       │    ├─ Card
       │    │    ├─ Label
       │    │    └─ SliderFloat
       │    └─ Card
       │         └─ Canvas
       ├─ PropertyGrid
       └─ NodeCanvasView
            └─ NodeElement
                 ├─ InputPin
                 └─ OutputPin
  • Objects are leaves: button, slider, label, checkbox, combo, canvas, node, pin, progress bar, badge, text.
  • Cards group objects on a raised surface: Card, Row, Column, Grid, Section, Toolbar, ScrollArea.
  • Panels are dockable windows: Panel, TabPage, NodeCanvasView, PropertyGrid.
  • App shells (PanelRegistry, Workspace, PluginManager) own panels and docking; they never draw controls by hand.

The kit is header-only (caffeine/ui/UI.hpp), so plugins can compose the same elements without linking the IDE. Underneath, each element still draws with ImGui; the tree gives stable ids, layout, debugging and a single visual language.

Main elements#

Group Elements
Containers Panel, Card, Row, Column, Grid, Section, Toolbar, ScrollArea, TabBar / TabPage, TreeView / TreeItem
Controls Button, IconButton, Checkbox, SliderFloat, SliderInt, DragFloat, DragInt, Combo, TextInput, SearchField, PathField, MultilineText, DropZone, ColorPicker, SegmentedControl
Lists & data ListItem, ListBox, AssetCard, DataTable / DataRow
Display Label / Text, Paragraph, Badge, StatusDot, ProgressBar, Separator, Spacer, Image, EmptyState, KeyValue
Properties PropertyGrid, PropertyRow, FloatProperty, IntProperty, BoolProperty, ChoiceProperty, ColorFieldProperty, Color3FieldProperty, TextFieldProperty, PathProperty, Vec2Property, Vec3Property
Canvas / nodes Canvas, CurveEditor, NodeCanvasView, NodeElement, InputPin, OutputPin
Overlays Dialog (modal body tree), CustomElement (host/legacy escape hatch)
Debug UIContext::debugDump(), UIContext::drawDebugOverlay(), DebugPanel

Example#

cpp
#include "caffeine/ui/UI.hpp"

using namespace Caffeine::UIKit;
using namespace Caffeine::UIKit::Elements;

Panel panel("My Tool", "Short description", "effects");
auto& card = panel.emplace<Card>("General");
card.emplace<Label>("Options", TextTone::Accent).setHeading(true);

auto& row = card.emplace<Row>("Actions");
row.emplace<Button>("Apply", ButtonVariant::Primary).setOnClick([&] { apply(); });
row.emplace<Button>("Cancel");

auto& grid = card.emplace<PropertyGrid>("Settings");
grid.typedRow<FloatProperty>("Amount", amount, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.01f, "%.2f", true);
grid.typedRow<BoolProperty>("Enabled", enabled);

UIContext ctx;
ctx.draw(panel);

A Row shares leftover width between setGrow(true) children; a Card sizes to its content; a PropertyGrid is just a two-column table of PropertyRows.

Canvas and nodes#

Canvas gives a draw callback with the origin and size of its surface. Use it for previews, graphs, timelines or any custom visual that should still participate in the element layout.

NodeCanvasView embeds the shared NodeCanvas and owns a list of NodeElements. Each node owns its body elements, including InputPin/OutputPin and normal controls. Links and graph semantics stay in the host tool.

Live catalogue#

Open View → Panels → UI Gallery (or run the UI Gallery command). The panel shows every element in context: buttons, inputs, text tones, badges, progress, property rows, a custom canvas, a node canvas and the element debug tree.

Enable Draw hit rectangles in its Debug card to see the bounds and ids of every element. UIContext::debugDump() returns the same information as text, which is useful in tests and bug reports.

Rules#

  1. A leaf draws one thing; a container owns layout.
  2. Use theme tokens, never hard-coded colors.
  3. Give dynamic list items explicit ids; static siblings can be auto-numbered.
  4. Keep graph/link/serialization logic in the host, not in NodeElement.
  5. Migrate one piece at a time: the older free-function widgets are still supported and are the low-level vocabulary underneath the elements.

The headers live in include/caffeine/ui/. This kit is the legacy ImGui plugin SDK vocabulary. The active Doppio editor is Rust/Iced and consumes the C ABI instead; see the Rust UI notes.
